mig_27k: The MiG-27K was Mikoyan's fully upgraded version of the swing-wing MiG-27 strike jet, built around the Kayra-23 laser-optical sight so it could use laser- and TV-guided weapons; its cost led the Soviet Air Force to halve the order and fill the rest with the cheaper MiG-27M. It is at home in both game modes: in air battles it can wipe out a base and still carry a complete air-to-air missile fit, with the same strong low-level performance as the MiG-27M, while in mixed battles its sight and guided arsenal make precise ground strikes easy. It arrived with the "Winged Lions" update.
mig_27m: The MiG-27M was the budget half of the late MiG-27 upgrade: it used a targeting system taken from the Su-17 family instead of the costly Kayra-23 of the MiG-27K, yet could still employ laser- and TV-guided weapons, and it served the USSR and export users in the 1980s. R-13M1 and R-60M missiles, a good stock of large countermeasures and a MiG-23BN-based airframe let it defend itself, but its real job is precision attack. It is the first aircraft on the Soviet bomber line with guided weapons, and with those plus the six-barrel GSh-6-30 cannon it is a dependable mixed-battle striker. It came in Update "Direct Hit".
mig_29_9_12: Mikoyan's light frontline fighter was conceived in the 1970s to work alongside the larger Su-27 and replace the MiG-23; it first flew in October 1977, and the 9-12 production model reached units in 1983, designed to be fast, agile and easy to maintain from rough airfields, though short on range. Quick, nimble and with a decent radar and helmet sight for its short- and medium-range missiles, it is held back by older missiles than later Fulcrums carry, notably R-60Ms that flares fool easily, and by having little to use on ground targets. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
mig_29_9_12_germany: East Germany bought 24 export-standard MiG-29 9-12A fighters in the 1980s, and after reunification the Luftwaffe kept them for more than a decade; a 1994 exercise against USAF F-16s at Aviano showed NATO how badly it had underrated the type, and in 2003 22 of them went to Poland for one euro apiece. For German pilots it is the first step into fourth-generation jets after the MiG-23MLA, adding the hard-hitting R-27ER1 and a helmet sight that allows its all-aspect heat-seekers to be fired well off the nose. It came with Update 2.25 "Sky Guardians".
mig_29_9_12_sniper: Romania's MiG-29 Sniper was an upgrade programme that would have given its Fulcrums Western avionics, including colour multifunction displays, a new HUD and an Elisra SPS-20(V) radar warning receiver, while keeping Soviet weapons; it was cancelled in favour of the MiG-21 LanceR. Sold as a premium pack in the Italian tree since the "Leviathans" update, it keeps the standard Fulcrum's flaws, a N019E radar that falls short of NATO equivalents and an airframe that bleeds energy against F-15s and F-16s. Its digital RWR is a real asset, naming radar types and warning of tracks and launches, and it fights with R-27ERs at range and R-60Ms plus a helmet sight up close.
mig_29_9_12b_hungary: Hungary received 28 MiG-29s of the 9-12B standard in 1993 as part of Russia's debt settlement, a big step up from its worn MiG-23MFs; after joining NATO in 1999 it moved to the Gripen and retired its last Fulcrum in December 2010. Found in the Hungarian part of the Italian tree, it gives players a differently flying option to the F-16A ADF. The long-reaching R-27ER1 and off-boresight shots with all-aspect IR missiles through a helmet sight are the big gains over the MiG-23MF before it. It arrived in Update 2.35 "Alpha Strike".
mig_29_9_12g: After reunification the Luftwaffe kept its ex-East German MiG-29s, which had outperformed most NATO fighters in testing, and upgraded them as the MiG-29G with Western avionics and NATO-compatible communications and navigation. In the game it keeps the familiar feel of the 9-12 but gains R-27ET1 and R-73E missiles. Next to the MiG-29SMT it gives up the newer radar, extra fuel and countermeasures and the guided ground weapons, and in return avoids that version's heavy weight, which makes it a lighter, more agile sidegrade. It was introduced in the "Kings of Battle" update.
mig_29_9_13: Shaped by Soviet lessons that agile fighters still mattered, Mikoyan's Fulcrum first flew in October 1977 with twin engines, a strong radar and a helmet-mounted sight for close combat; the 9-13 entered production in 1986 with a larger fuel bulge behind the cockpit and reshaped wingtips. When added in Update "Apex Predators" it became the Soviet tree's first fourth-generation fighter, and it plays almost exactly like the 9-12. Its jump over the MiG-23 is large: the radar is a genuine pulse-Doppler set, the R-27ER ranks among the strongest radar-guided missiles, and the helmet sight lets R-60M and R-27T shots go well off the nose.
mig_29kr_9_41r: The carrier-based MiG-29K, derived from the MiG-29M, first landed on the carrier now called Admiral Kuznetsov in 1989 but was shelved after the Soviet collapse; revived by an Indian order, it returned for the Russian Navy, which contracted 20 single-seat MiG-29KRs in 2012 and used them against targets in Syria in 2016. A larger wing and more powerful engines set it apart from the MiG-29M. It relies on R-77s and R-73s against aircraft, with no R-27 option, while Kh-31A/P and TV-guided Kh-29 missiles give it real punch against ground targets, so it suits air and mixed battles alike. It was added in Update 2.57 "Heavy Cavalry".
mig_29m_9_15: A deep redesign of the Fulcrum begun in the mid-1980s, the MiG-29M gained a reworked airframe with more fuel, fly-by-wire controls and the N010 Zhuk radar, opening up R-77 missiles and precision strike weapons; six prototypes flew, but early-1990s budget cuts stopped production, and the design fed into the MiG-29K and MiG-35. Its headline feature is room for eight R-77s, a big step beyond the 9-13 and SMT, backed by up to four TV-guided Kh-29TDs for strikes. RD-33K engines claw back some of the added weight, but a small flare supply and no targeting pod hold it back. It arrived in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave".
mig_29n: Malaysia ordered 18 MiG-29s in 1994, took delivery in 1995 and later upgraded them locally towards the 9.12SD standard with in-flight refuelling, a better radar and RVV-AE missiles; they served until 2017, when the Su-30MKM replaced them. In the Japanese tree its powerful engines make it fast and nimble, and RVV-AE active radar missiles give an otherwise early Fulcrum real reach. The trade-offs are old avionics and a ground-attack fit of rockets, napalm and unguided bombs that does little against armour. It came in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact".
mig_29smt_9_19: With Russia's next-generation fighter programmes stalled for lack of money, RSK MiG revived its 1990s MiG-29SMT modernisation as a cheaper answer to late F-16s and the new European canard fighters; the 9-19 standard was finalised in 2006 and serves with Russia, Algeria and Syria. R-77 active radar missiles, better radar and avionics, and a broad set of guided air-to-ground weapons make it far deadlier than the MiG-29 (9-13), although it handles noticeably worse. It was added in Update 2.29 "Sons of Attila".
mig_35: A "4++ generation" development of the MiG-29M and MiG-29K, the MiG-35 adds an AESA radar, a new helmet display and more guided strike weapons; it first flew in January 2017, and Russia took its first two production jets in 2019. In the game it climbs fast, is quick high up and turns at subsonic speed as sharply as any Fulcrum, carrying R-77-1 and R-73 missiles cued by that radar and helmet sight for short- and medium-range fights. Kh-38ML/MT missiles and guided bombs make it dangerous in mixed battles, but fuel is tight and has to be watched. It came in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
mig_3_series_1_15: Designed by Mikoyan-Gurevich as a high-altitude interceptor, the MiG-3 could outpace the Bf 109 at around 6,000 m, though its AM-35A engine left it slower near sea level. In the game it is one of the first fighters able to reach high-flying bombers, and it works best climbing early and diving on targets below rather than turning, as its controls are stiff and it is less agile than its rivals. Its nose guns, one 12.7 mm and two 7.62 mm, are easy to aim without convergence settings but lack punch, so the engine, pilot and fuel tanks are the targets to aim for. It was added in Update 1.31.
mig_3_series_1_15_bk_pod: This MiG-3-15 variant differs from the standard aircraft only in two extra non-synchronised 12.7 mm Berezin UB guns, giving it three UBs and two 7.62 mm ShKAS behind a 1,200 hp Mikulin AM-35A. Its three UBs are the largest such battery used as main armament on any aircraft in the game; the gun outpaces the American M2 Browning in rate of fire and muzzle velocity, and short bursts at wings or engines bring down light fighters, though bombers soak up hits better. Like the base MiG-3 it is an energy fighter suited to boom-and-zoom, quite unlike the I-16 line before it. It arrived in Update 1.37.
mig_3_series_34: An experimental MiG-3 variant meant to fix the series' weak firepower, the MiG-3-34 came from a high-altitude design that struggled in service with poor build quality and oxygen supply, and in 1941 it met agile Bf 109s instead of bombers before Yak and LaGG fighters replaced it. Above 4,000 m its engine reaches full power, and that is where it belongs: hunting bombers and fighting on speed and acceleration in the manner of the I-185 and I-225, rather than turning or trading fire with Spitfires and Bf 109s, which outclass it in agility and firepower. It arrived in Update 1.41.
mirage_2000_5eg_mk2_greece: Greece ordered 40 Mirage 2000s in 1985 and in the early 2000s upgraded part of the fleet and bought 15 more to the 2000-5 Mk.2 standard, with RDY-2 radar, modern avionics and MICA missiles; the Rafale is now replacing them. Functionally a copy of the French Mirage 2000-5F, it pairs MICA-EM missiles at medium range with R550 Magic 2s for close fights, while its delta wing and strong engine make it agile and quick, though it bleeds speed in long turning fights. Against ground targets it has nothing but anti-radiation missiles. It was added to the Israeli tree in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey".
mirage_2000_5ei: Taiwan's air force, unable to buy F-4s or F-16s from the US in the 1980s to replace ageing F-104s and F-5s, turned to France and received Mirage 2000-5Ei fighters from 1997 with ground-attack capability removed; the deal helped push Washington into selling F-16s from 1998. In the Chinese tree it is essentially a single-seat Mirage 2000-5F without strike weapons. Outranged by opponents such as the F-15E and the J-10A it faced in reality, it is at its best cleaning up the last enemy jets late in a match with its MICA-EM missiles and good electronics. It arrived in Update "Firebirds".
mirage_2000_5f: Dassault's Mirage 2000-5F, first flown in 1991, brought upgraded avionics and weapons to the Mirage 2000 line and flew both air-to-air and ground-attack sorties over Kosovo in 1999. In the game it is above all an air-superiority jet: agile enough to gain the upper hand in a turning fight, it uses the Thales RDY radar to find and track several targets quickly and finishes them at close range with the infrared-guided Matra Magic 2. It came to the game in the "La Royale" update.
mirage_2000c_s4: Dassault's Mirage 2000 first flew in 1978 after the AFVG and Mirage G projects failed, and the C ("Chasseur") version long served as France's main interceptor. The C-S4 arrived in Update "Air Superiority" as a reward from the 2023 Winter Extreme event and is nearly identical to the tech-tree C-S5, but has fewer countermeasures and no missile approach warning. In practice the two fly the same way: its performance lets it decide when to fight, with Super 530D radar missiles for longer shots and all-aspect R.550 Magic 2s up close.
mirage_2000c_s5: The penultimate Mirage 2000C standard added the uprated M53-P2 engine, an Eclair chaff and flare dispenser and the improved RDI radar for the Super 530D missile, bringing it level with contemporary MiG-29s and F-16s. Its light airframe and strong engine are the selling points: it accelerates hard, reaches high speeds and pulls a high angle of attack, and although the delta sheds energy at low speed it regains it quickly. The missile and bomb load is smaller than rivals', and the 530D is no match for late AIM-7s or R-27s at range, so it does best kept low, using the IRCCM-equipped Magic 2 inside about 3 km. It arrived in Update "Drone Age".
mirage_2000d_r1: Descended from the nuclear-strike Mirage 2000N by way of the 2000D, the D-R1 is a two-seat ground-attack Mirage with improved countermeasures, ECM and RWR, plus AS-30L missiles, laser-guided bombs and a targeting pod. Its guided weapons are accurate but few, two GBU-12s and two AS-30Ls alongside a pair of Magic 2s, so it fits ground battles best, bombing from altitude first and then using the AS-30L, whose HE warhead is better spent on distant SPAA than on tanks. Despite the extra weight, the 2000C-family engine gives brisk low-speed acceleration and a high top speed, at the cost of thirsty fuel use. It arrived in Update "Apex Predators".
mirage_2000d_rmv: Dassault's mid-life renovation programme, launched in 2015, gave the strike Mirage new avionics and a wider range of weapons, with upgraded aircraft reaching units from 2022 and 55 planned to keep the type flying into the 2030s. Its game role is unchanged from the D-R1, a strike specialist that struggles against aircraft, but the weapon list grows: the DAMOCLES pod and GBU-48, GBU-49 and GBU-50 bombs with both satellite and laser guidance join the older stores. It came in Update 2.41 "Firebirds".
mirage_3c: The first production Mirage III, the IIIC was a delta-wing interceptor and dogfighter with an afterburning Atar 09B, DEFA 30 mm cannons and, at first, AIM-9B Sidewinders; 95 were built and it served until 1988. Its game kit follows the usual French delta pattern of 30 mm cannon, a strong engine and Magic 1 heat-seekers, with R530E radar missiles for medium range, though the radar is only really useful at high altitude. Without flares and with mediocre acceleration, it should avoid being tied up near several enemies, keeping its speed high and saving Magic 1s for shots inside about 2 km. It arrived in Update "Starfighters".
mirage_3cj: The Shahak was Israel's Mirage IIICJ and its first Mach 2 fighter, the main air superiority aircraft through the Six-Day and Yom Kippur wars, where pilots often trusted the DEFA cannons over unreliable missiles; 72 served before the Kfir and F-4 took over. Its flight model is close to the French Mirage IIIC, but American AIM-9Ds replace the Magic 1s. Speed is its main defence, since it carries no countermeasures and accelerates sluggishly at low speed, and while it turns sharply and pulls a high angle of attack, it bleeds energy doing so. It came with the "Winged Lions" update.
mirage_3e: Built as a more multirole partner to the interceptor Mirage IIIC, the IIIE added a British pulse-Doppler navigation radar under the cockpit, more fuel, a newer ATAR 09 engine and better avionics; with 192 built for the French Air Force, it was the most produced Mirage III by 1971. Where the IIIC is a pure interceptor, the IIIE can also attack ground targets, with a ballistic computer aiding gun, rocket and bomb runs. It adds an RWR and countermeasures too, and its revised Atar 9 answers the throttle far faster while giving slightly more thrust. It arrived in Update "Ixwa Strike".
mirage_3s_c70_switzerland: Switzerland chose the Mirage IIIC as its first supersonic fighter and built it under licence as the Mirage IIIS, though funding cut production from 100 to 54; from 1988 the fleet gained canards (C.70 stands for "canard wing at 70%") and new avionics, and most retired in 1999. In the German tree the Swiss upgrades give it an edge over the French IIIC in avionics and missiles, notably the semi-active AIM-26 and a licence-built AIM-9E, and besides the SEPR844 rocket booster it can use new JATO rockets. Against that, it sheds speed heavily in turns and has no air-to-ground armament. It was added in Update 2.47 "Leviathans".
mirage_4000: Dassault's private-venture Mirage 4000, essentially a twin-engined, canard-equipped Mirage 2000 scaled up to rival the F-15, found no buyer: France judged it too expensive and export prospects fell through, so the single prototype ended up in a Paris museum in 1992, its lessons passing to the Rafale. Few French aircraft are as versatile: four Super 530Ds and a strong radar handle longer-range work, as many as eight Magic 2s cover the close fights it already excels in, and the ATLIS pod with laser-guided bombs and missiles makes it a serious attacker. It came in Update "Air Superiority" and will feel familiar to Mirage 2000 pilots.
mirage_5ba: Belgium ordered Mirage 5s in 1968 to replace its F-84F and RF-84F jets, with 54 of the planned 88 being Mirage 5BA fighters fitted with American electronics; after the Cold War, Chile bought 20 of them, naming them Elkan. What sets it apart from the French Mirage 5F in the game is a countermeasure dispenser. Otherwise it is a nimble fighter whose missiles are effective but few, with a modest cannon ammunition supply and no guided air-to-ground weapons. It came in Update 2.37 "Seek & Destroy".
mirage_5f: The Mirage 5 was a stripped-down Mirage III requested by Israel, trading radar and avionics for extra fuel; France's 1967 arms embargo blocked delivery of the 50 ordered, and Israel, after taking a refund, built its own copy, the Nesher, from blueprints obtained through espionage. It shares its airframe with the Nesher but swaps Shafrir 2s for AIM-9Bs and Magic 1s. With no radar, no countermeasures and just two short-range missiles, it does best as a fast base bomber that avoids enemies carrying all-aspect missiles and uses its speed and brief dogfighting ability to catch the unwary. It came in the "Winged Lions" update.
